name: moduletto (NEON i16 ML-KEM-512)
workload: Full ML-KEM-512 KEM session (keygen+encaps+decaps), 10,000 iterations/100-iteration warmup, ACVP FIPS 203 conformant, on Apple M5 NEON
claimed_speedup: ~1.18x faster full-session throughput than LibOQS 0.16.0 (13.7-14.1us vs 16.19us total time; ~72,000 vs 61,800 sessions/sec) and faster in all three phases (keygen 4.07 vs 4.72us, encaps 3.84 vs 5.25us, decaps 5.80 vs 6.22us); 2.96x vs Kyber C reference at 47.87us (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: moduletto: rustc, Criterion 0.7, `examples/kyber_benchmark` release build; LibOQS: `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DOQS_MINIMAL_BUILD=KEM_ml_kem_512 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-O3 -march=native"` built from tag 0.16.0
tradeoffs: NEON-only fast path (i64 NTT + SHA3/inline-Keccak backends are 2.5-3x slower fallbacks for non-ARM); single-developer project, no independent security review; author's own doc flags that fixing FIPS 203 conformance bugs (found via ACVP vectors) was what got it under LibOQS, not the SIMD work alone
caveats: Margin over LibOQS is small (1.18x) and the author explicitly notes LibOQS 0.16.0 is itself 1.26x faster than 0.15.0, so comparisons against older LibOQS releases overstate the lead; the Kyber-C-reference column was carried over from an earlier session and not re-measured in this run; license is PolyForm Noncommercial (non-OSI), so it is usable for study/evaluation but not for commercial redistribution without a separate license
found_via: GitHub code search: "vs liboqs" -> crabnebula-dev/moduletto BENCHMARKS.md

name: sntrup (Streamlined NTRU Prime, pure Rust)
baseline: liboqs (sntrup761, AVX2-dispatched SUPERCOP backend on x86_64 / portable C on aarch64) and PQClean sntrup761 C reference
workload: sntrup761 keypair generation, encapsulation and decapsulation, Criterion benchmarks run in the same process against liboqs (oqs-sys) and PQClean (pqcrypto-ntruprime) in benches/comparison
claimed_speedup: On aarch64 (Apple M2 Max, both refs' portable/NEON-less C paths): keypair 25% faster (1.341ms vs 1.780/1.827ms), encapsulate ~3% faster (50.00us vs 51.54/51.39us), decapsulate ~6% faster (84.52us vs 90.20/90.54us) than both PQClean and liboqs. On x86_64 (Zen 5) it beats PQClean's C reference by 10.0x/7.3x/11.6x on the three operations, but liboqs's AVX2/SUPERCOP kernel still wins there by 3.3x/2.8x/6.3x
compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.97.1 (aarch64 run) / rustc 1.98.0-nightly (x86_64 run), cargo release profile, default features except pqcrypto-ntruprime's avx2 feature left off; oqs-sys built from vendored liboqs source
hardware: Apple M2 Max, macOS (aarch64); AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 'Strix Point' Zen 5, Fedora Linux, pinned to one 5.16GHz core via taskset (x86_64)
tradeoffs: Pure Rust with automatic AVX-512/AVX2/AVX-VNNI/NEON runtime dispatch; on x86_64 it does not beat liboqs's hand-tuned AVX2 SUPERCOP kernel, only PQClean's plain C; every secret-derived buffer is zeroized (a security win over the C references, which don't wipe), at a measured ~11% throughput cost that is included in the reported numbers
caveats: The 'beats liboqs' framing only holds on aarch64, where liboqs has no NEON-specific sntrup761 path and falls back to portable C; on x86_64, where liboqs dispatches to its optimized AVX2 code, liboqs remains 2.8x-6.3x faster than this crate for sntrup761. Zero GitHub stars and a single maintainer, but the repo's RESULTS.md is an unusually rigorous same-run engineering log with stated compiler, flags and CPU model for every figure
found_via: GitHub code search: "faster than PQClean" -> mikelodder7/sntrup CHANGELOG.md and benches/comparison/RESULTS.md
